\section{Materials and methods}

\subsection{Overview}

pgphase takes the reads' alignments to a pangenome graph, as a GAF file \citep{Li2020}, the graph's site catalog and, optionally, the same reads aligned to the linear reference, as a BAM file (Fig.~\ref{fig:overview}). It processes the reference in chunks (1~Mb by default when a BAM is given) in parallel and joins adjacent chunks through the reads they share. It has two parts: the \emph{graph arm}, which phases the catalog's sites from the graph alignments, and \emph{union gap phasing}, which adds the sample's own heterozygous variants from the linear alignments and phases all sites in one solve. It writes a phased VCF and the reads' haplotype (HP) and phase set (PS) tags. All thresholds below were set on the development chromosomes (Section 2.8); Supplementary Table S5 lists every one with its value.

\input{figures/overview}

\subsection{Site catalog and read evidence from a pangenome graph}

The catalog is built once per graph, from a GBZ graph \citep{Siren2022} with \texttt{build-snarl-catalog}: each snarl \citep{Paten2018} of the graph is a site, whose reference allele is the walk of the reference path through it and whose alternative alleles are the distinct walks of the haplotype paths, ordered by the number of haplotypes that take them. The reads' graph alignments are indexed once by reference position (\texttt{index-gaf}). For each chunk, every read with mapping quality 5 or more (1 or more when a BAM is given) that crosses a site contributes the allele whose walk its alignment follows. An allele is identified by its walk, so two reads carry the same allele exactly when they take the same path through the site. A multi-allelic site is split into one reference-against-alternative contrast per alternative allele, and sites are filtered by depth and allele fraction. Indels in homopolymers, tandem repeats and low-complexity sequence are classified as noisy and left out of the first solve.

\subsection{Phasing the catalog sites}

The catalog's clean heterozygous sites are phased first by k-means clustering of the reads on their alleles, the algorithm of longcallD \citep{Gao2026} applied to walk observations. With a BAM, each catalog SNP is tested against the aligned bases of reads of mapping quality 30 or more: a SNP whose reference base is absent from these reads (a binomial test, Bonferroni-corrected at 1\% over the chunk's SNPs) and whose absence no deletion explains is reclassified as homozygous. Where the two alleles of a SNP site differ at a single node of the graph, a read whose walk follows another allele of the snarl takes the SNP allele whose node that walk contains, when it contains exactly one of them; reads on rarer walks through the site thus still contribute. The labels of this clean solve initialise the joint solve below.

\subsection{The sample's own heterozygous variants}

With a BAM, each chunk is also solved from its linear alignments by the alignment pipeline pgphase ports from longcallD \citep{Gao2026}: candidate variants are collected from the reads' differences to the reference and classified by depth, allele fraction and sequence context, and noisy regions of up to 2~kb are resolved by aligning each haplotype's reads with partial order alignment \citep{Gao2021}. Its clean heterozygous variants, and the noisy-region variants the multiple sequence alignment verifies, join the chunk's sites with their per-read alleles. A verified noisy variant must be observed by at least two reads of mapping quality 30 or more on each of its two alleles, and no site observed by more than 1.5 times the chunk's median depth is added: at a collapsed duplication the two ``alleles'' are the copies, and a run of such sites is perfectly consistent with itself. Verified noisy variants that fail these rules are still used, but only to label reads as islands (Section 2.7). A clean call inside a noisy region longer than the MSA limit cannot be verified; it is kept as an \emph{unverified} call, which takes no part in joins and labels reads only as a last resort (Section 2.7). Placements of one indel at different copies of a repeat are merged into one site; a call inside a catalog site of up to 2~kb only supplies alleles to reads the graph left without one there, and one inside a longer site is added as a site of its own; and reads with mapping quality 20 or more that only the linear alignment holds are added. At each added indel, every read that crosses the site without a call is realigned to the two alleles in reference context and takes the closer one, with a per-read error of \(1/(1+e^{3m})\) for a margin of \(m\) edits; where the MSA called the read, its call is kept, with error 0.25 if realignment cannot decide and 0.35 if it calls the other allele. Where a read's allele at a catalog SNP disagrees with its aligned base, the base is used: measured against the parents on the development chromosomes, the aligned base was correct in 88--93\% of such disagreements. A graph allele at a SNP whose base the read's alignment does not give keeps an error of 0.25.

\subsection{One expectation-maximization over all sites}

Every site with two observed alleles, from the catalog or the sample, is given a phase \(h_s\in\{0,1\}\) and an error rate \(\varepsilon_s\), and every read \(r\) a posterior probability for each haplotype. With \(x_{rs}\in\{0,1\}\) the allele read \(r\) shows at site \(s\) and \(e_{rs}\) the per-read error of that call (zero when none is known), a read from haplotype \(a\) has likelihood

\begin{equation}
L_r(a) = \prod_{s} \bigl(1-\varepsilon_{rs}\bigr)^{[x_{rs} = h_s \oplus a]}\, \varepsilon_{rs}^{[x_{rs} \neq h_s \oplus a]},
\end{equation}

where \(\varepsilon_{rs} = 1-(1-\varepsilon_s)(1-e_{rs})\) combines the error of the site with that of the call. Expectation-maximization \citep{Dempster1977} alternates between the reads' posteriors and the sites' phases and errors, starting from error 0.05 at clean sites and 0.2 at the others and from the clean solve's labels; site errors are kept between 0.01 and 0.45. The error of a site is the weighted disagreement of its reads, shrunk by five pseudo-reads toward the median error of the sites of its class in the chunk that carry at least ten reads' teaching weight (the weighted mean when fewer than five such sites exist) (clean catalog heterozygotes, other catalog sites, added variants, local windows and unverified calls from noisy regions longer than 2~kb, each divided by whether the site is a one-base length difference). This empirical Bayes prior keeps, for example, a noisy homopolymer call from overruling a clean SNP that shares its reads. Only reads of mapping quality 20 or more update the model; the others are scored against it and labelled. A read whose calls all lie at one site does not teach that site's error, since its posterior comes from the site alone, except at clean catalog heterozygotes, whose starting error is the better prior. A site whose rarer allele is held by fewer than a quarter of its reads is left out, since such a skewed split is typical of a paralogous copy or of an error. After 15 iterations, the solve flips all sites beyond the boundary whose flip most increases the likelihood, for as long as some flip increases it (at most 30 rounds). A site whose learned error is 0.3 or more is reported unphased and labels no read, and a read is labelled in the block where its evidence is strongest if its posterior there is at least 0.8.

\subsection{Joining blocks only where reads verify the join}

A block ends wherever flipping all sites beyond a boundary would cost less than 4 log-likelihood units, or where fewer than two reads carry evidence on both sides, since a single molecule can be chimeric or misplaced. The cut is judged over all reads, including those below mapping quality 20: a read too ambiguously mapped to shape the model still shows that its molecule continues across the boundary. Because a wrong join misphases every read beyond it, pgphase further restricts which sites can support a join:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{One-base length differences are weak.} A homopolymer length call in a homozygous stretch can look heterozygous. Where the join margin from the other sites alone is below 4, a join that relies on such sites needs a margin of 10 log-likelihood units.
  \item \textbf{Strong joins need several reads.} A margin counts as strong only when at least four reads carry evidence at reliable, non-weak sites on both sides of the boundary.
  \item \textbf{Collapsed duplications and poorly mapped sites support no joins.} A site called by more than twice the chunk's median number of reads, by more than 1.3 times that number with its rarer allele below 40\%, or by reads whose mean mapping quality is below 40, labels reads but supports no join.
  \item \textbf{Redundant evidence counts once.} In the join test, a read's call at a site inside a local window is ignored when the read also has a call at the window. A site within 30~bp of another that shares at least 80\% of its reads, 95\% of which split the same way at both, repeats that site's evidence and does not vote on read labels.
  \item \textbf{No hinges.} A site that alone connects two blocks through weak joins on both sides, with no read spanning it, is cut at the weaker join.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Labels for the remaining reads, and output}

Reads that the solve leaves unlabelled are labelled from evidence the solve does not vote with. Local haplotype windows, up to 2~kb long, contrast the two haplotype sequences of a noisy locus, each the medoid of reads labelled on one side; allele windows contrast the two exact alleles of a heterozygous indel the solve does not observe, including two-allele sites with no reference read; and length windows genotype tandem repeat tracts under a stutter model learned from the chunk. A second pass of the solve uses haplotype and allele windows as sites. After the solve, adjacent chunks are joined in the orientation supported by the reads they share, only when one orientation leads by at least three reads and 90\%. Sites left out of the solve are then oriented from the labelled reads when their alleles associate with one phase set (exact one-sided binomial test, \(p \le 0.01\)), and label the unlabelled reads that cross them, using a read's linear-alignment allele where its graph alignment gives none. Last, a read whose calls in a block all agree takes the block's label if its posterior there is at least 0.7, and a read still unlabelled is phased by its own call at one site that cannot vote, in a block of that site alone (an \emph{island}), which joins nothing, so that a wrong island affects only its own reads. Island sites are the sites the solve rejected, repeat indels it never sees, verified noisy variants that failed the rules of Section 2.4, and length windows; a site must be called by two unlabelled reads and have both alleles in at least a quarter of its reads, and a read takes the one with the lowest error. Before islands, a read with only unverified calls takes their label at posterior 0.8 when their learned error is below 0.1. In the VCF, multi-base substitutions are written as their single-base changes, indels are left-aligned, and two records of one variant are collapsed, keeping the phased one; a phase set whose heterozygotes all lie at one locus (within 10~bp) is written unphased, as are SNPs of learned error 0.1 or more, indels of 0.25 or more and unverified calls.

\subsection{Evaluation}

\textbf{Data.} HG002 \citep{Zook2016} PacBio HiFi reads (DRAFT: source and chemistry) were aligned with vg Giraffe v1.73.0 \citep{Siren2021,Chang2025}, in its HiFi preset with minimizers \(k=31\) and \(w=50\), to a 16-haplotype sample \citep{Siren2024} of the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium release 2 Minigraph-Cactus graph on CHM13 \citep{Liao2023,Hickey2024,HPRC2}, from which HG002 and its parents had been removed (229 assembled samples, CHM13 and GRCh38), and the alignments were surjected onto CHM13 \citep{Nurk2022}; they covered chr19 at 59-fold. The site catalog was built from the full graph rather than from the 16-haplotype sample. All tools received the same reads: pgphase their graph alignments and the surjected BAM, the other tools the BAM. HiPhase 1.6.0, LongPhase 2.0.2 and WhatsHap 2.8, run by default and with \texttt{-{}-distrust-genotypes} (WhatsHap-dg), phased DeepVariant 1.10.0 calls (PACBIO model) made on the same BAM; longcallD v0.0.11 called and phased its own. pgphase was developed on chr12, chr17, chr18, chr19 and chr20, whose truth guided its rules and thresholds. chr6, chr16 and chr21 were not used to choose thresholds; they were scored during development to check that changes generalised, and one rule (the hinge rule, Section 2.6) was found by examining an error on chr6. The MHC (chr6:28.5--34.0~Mb) is reported separately.

\textbf{Truth.} The reads were aligned separately to the maternal and the paternal haplotype of the HG002 v1.1 assembly \citep{Hansen2025} with minimap2 2.31 \citep{Li2018} (preset \texttt{lr:hqae}, no secondary alignments). HipHap \citep{HipHap} compared the two alignments of each read, assigned the read to the haplotype with the better alignment score and scored the assignment's confidence (HapQ), using minimap2's match score rather than an estimate from a random sample of reads, so that the labels are reproducible. Reads without a parental label are not scored. Truth heterozygous variants are those of the Q100 HG002 small-variant benchmark on CHM13 \citep{Hansen2025}.

\textbf{Read metrics.} A primary read is \emph{phaseable} when its alignment spans a heterozygous truth variant. Each phase set takes the parental orientation of the majority of its truth-labelled reads; a read is \emph{correct} when its haplotype tag agrees with that orientation, \emph{discordant} when it does not, and \emph{unphased} when it has no tag. A read is centromeric when its alignment midpoint lies in one interval per chromosome spanning its centromeric and pericentromeric satellites, as annotated on CHM13 \citep{Altemose2022} and listed in Supplementary Table S4, and on the arms otherwise. One region at the end of chr20 where the truth labels contradict the truth variants is not scored (Supplementary Table S4). We also report the discordant reads whose parental assignment is confident (HapQ $\ge$ 30): on the development chromosomes, every tool was 25--37\% discordant on reads below HapQ 10, most of which carry the other parent's alleles at their own clean SNVs, which points to an error in the label rather than in the phase. All tools were scored by the same script.

\textbf{Variant metrics.} A tool's phased heterozygous biallelic records are matched to the truth by position, reference and alternative allele. Within a phase set, a single matched heterozygote whose orientation disagrees with agreeing neighbours on both sides is a \emph{flip}, and a lasting change of orientation is a \emph{switch}. Switches and flips are counted separately on the arms and in the centromeric intervals. In repeats, the same haplotypes can be written as different records, and a record-level comparison then counts switches where the haplotypes agree. We therefore classify each switch by sequence: around each of the two heterozygotes bounding it, a window of 75~bp on either side, extended until no record of either VCF crosses its edges (at most 20~kb), the tool's two haplotype sequences are compared with the truth's by edit distance, and each window pairs them in the cheaper way. A switch is \emph{real} when the two windows pair the haplotypes in opposite ways, \emph{representation} when both pair them the same way, and \emph{undecided} when the two pairings of either window differ by less than 30\% (or by fewer than 2 edits). A phase set spans from its first to its last phased heterozygous record; we report the number of phase sets and the N50 (not NG50) of their spans. Running time and peak memory were measured with GNU time on one machine with an Intel Core i9-7900X processor (10 cores) and 91~GB of memory.

\subsection{Implementation}

pgphase is written in C++17 on htslib, with abPOA \citep{Gao2021} for partial order alignment, WFA2-lib and edlib for pairwise alignment; its alignment pipeline is derived from longcallD \citep{Gao2026}, whose MIT-licensed code it ports and tests against. Catalog building and GAF indexing are done by pgcat, a Rust program that reads the GBZ graph with the gbz library \citep{Siren2022}. Chunks are processed by a pool of worker threads, each with its own file handles, and joined in one sequential pass; output does not depend on the number of threads.
